summary: Jefferson County, WA coast cabin built in 1942 for the Air Warning Service, abandoned in 1944, now gone; only buried remnants are described.

facts.status_note: Cabin gone; WillhiteWeb describes only buried remnants (boards, nails, hinges, glass)

facts.agency: Built for the Air Warning Service; register administrator is Washington Division of Forestry/DNR

visit.trail_note: A 3.5-mile trail was built to reach the site in 1942 (WillhiteWeb); no source describes a trail today

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 1,214 ft (370 m); firelookout.com gives 1058 ft; WillhiteWeb gives 1,000 ft. The story keeps the register figure, which matches our record.
Forest Lookouts quotes a May 1944 AWS report giving 12 x 16; WillhiteWeb quotes a December 1942 AWS list giving 12x36. Not reconciled; the story reports both.
Forest Lookouts lists deactivation on March 15, 1944 and, separately, a station deactivated March 20, 1944; WillhiteWeb gives 3/20/1944. The story says March 1944 and notes both dates.
Register lists Washington Division of Forestry/DNR as the current administrator; the 1942 AWS list places the station on Park Service land. These describe different periods, not a contradiction.

Forest Lookouts gives February 2, 1943 as the activation date; WillhiteWeb's master map labels the same date as the inactivation date. Not reconciled; the story reports Forest Lookouts' date and notes WillhiteWeb's label.

notes_for_editor: Brief coordinates (47.76595, -124.41928, from the firelookout.org Washington list) differ from the FFLOS detail page (47.768050, -124.411940), about 0.6 km apart; the story does not use coordinates. No access level is given: no source says whether the public may visit, so facts.access is omitted. The only source for remnants today is WillhiteWeb, which refers to 2017. Brief's elevation of 370 m matches the register. No new photos found. The register and the AWS lists describe one cabin; the story keeps both labels.
